en.title: Common mistakes in Horizon Europe project websites
en.lead: Three recurring patterns in Horizon Europe project websites, and how to avoid them.

sections.heading: Treating the website as a one-off deliverable
paragraphs: When a project website is treated as a launch deliverable rather than a living tool, it ages quickly. The most common consequence is a structure that cannot absorb new deliverables, results or events without manual intervention from a developer.

sections.heading: Overloaded homepages
paragraphs: Project homepages often try to communicate every aspect of the project at once. A clearer approach is to use the homepage to orient visitors (who this is, what it does, where to go next) and let dedicated pages carry the depth.

sections.heading: Hidden deliverables and publications
paragraphs: Deliverables and publications are often a primary reason visitors arrive on a project website. They should be easy to find, well structured and consistently presented across the project lifecycle.

meta.title: Common mistakes in Horizon Europe project websites | TechPi
meta.description: Three recurring mistakes in Horizon Europe project websites: one-off launch builds, overloaded homepages and hidden deliverables, and how to avoid each of them.
